name: Bryn Talle
aliases: the only name on the roll

identity.realm: Eighth gate, and the eighth is where mortals stop, which is a limit nobody was ever issued

appearance.presentation: An ordinary woman of entirely ordinary face, which in a setting where almost everybody is visibly something is the most conspicuous thing she can be. She dresses the way a household dresses when nobody has decided what it is yet, and she is the only person in most rooms who does not read as a specimen.
appearance.age: Thirty-four, which is young enough that the setting has not yet finished deciding what she is for.
appearance.build: Unremarkable and unadapted, the frame of somebody who has done a variety of manual work without ever being asked to specialise in any of it.
appearance.complexion: Ordinary warm human skin, wind-bitten and sun-marked in a way that does not read as anything but weather.
appearance.hair: Brown, cut at the jaw in no style at all, tied back when she is working and loose when she is not, because she has never had an occasion that justified more.
appearance.eyes: Brown, unremarkable, and extremely quick — the one part of her that has clearly been trained, and trained at something other than a gate.
appearance.palette: Undifferentiated: brown wool, grey linen, a leather belt, and nothing on her that was chosen for any reason other than availability.
appearance.attire: A work coat with the hem mended four times, a belt carrying a roll of paper rather than tools, and hard shoes resoled until the soles are smoother than the uppers.
appearance.marks: A March brand on the inside of her left wrist, half worn away, which she has not had removed and does not cover.
appearance.bearing: Straight-backed and unperformative, with the habit of standing where she can see every door, which is a levy's habit rather than a household's.

canon.role_in_story: The Standing Name is a mutual society on the principle that a community's promise is re-made jointly once a year and never priced, and it is the only form of insurance available to a population with no wealth. She keeps it, which means every year she has to stand in front of everyone and re-promise on their behalf that the household will stand behind them. This year the household is on the March's roll of the absent, and she is the only name on that roll that came back.
canon.first_appearance: First seen standing at the edge of a standing-name circle with a roll of paper in one hand and her wrist turned deliberately outward, waiting to be asked whether the household can still keep a promise.
canon.lore: A Commonborn is the body everyone is born into before the world has an opinion of them. It stops where mortals stop and lends no discipline, which is exactly why it is weak: nothing about its anatomy favours a path, so it must settle on one early and is weakest precisely where a specialist is strongest, and the mind path is closed to it outright. She settled on qi, cleared the eighth gate, and is now the most capable generalist in a household of specialists.
history: Born in Quartermark, the mortal world that holds a hundred and admits plants and beasts, and is therefore the only tier on which this body is not a visitor.

Levied with the March at sixteen, which the March may call and may not own, and entered nowhere, and walked back nine years later because the muster that would have written her down as dead never happened.
Came home to discover that a roll kept by a levy company is paid per name and grows without ever closing, and that she is the only entry on it with a household that still exists.

Settled on the qi path late and cleared the eighth gate, which is where mortals stop, having been told by an instructor that a commonborn frame has no discipline to lend and would need to find its own.
Took the Standing Name's keeping after the household's last competent member was levied, because the promise has to be re-made by somebody present and she was the only one who was.

Found, on re-reading the roll, that the March has already drawn a death payment against her name, which means the money arrived, which means somebody was recorded dead who was not, and she has spent the season trying to decide whether returning it would close the roll or falsify it.

personality.summary: Competent, plain-spoken, and quietly astonished that she is the important one. She has spent nine years being an absence and has not entirely finished being one. She does the job she is given without complaint and is far better at it than anyone expected, and she has never once brought that up.

personality.voice: Plain, level and entirely without performance. Says exactly what a thing is and no more, because she grew up in a household where a summary was worth less than a figure. Speaks in the present tense about things that have already happened, which is a levy's habit she never lost.

relationships.note: A community's promise is re-made jointly once a year and never priced, and it is the only insurance available to a population with no wealth. She is the person who has to stand up and say it out loud on their behalf, and this year the household it is made for is two-thirds absent.

A levy company is paid per name and keeps a roll of people who were levied and neither returned nor recorded dead, so the roll grows and nothing on it closes. She walked back off it, which makes her the only entry in the setting with a proof of return attached, and the single most unwelcome fact anyone on the roll could hold.

The March's claim is institutional and its standing is earned and the two never read each other, so the claim is held together by a roll kept in the heads of the people. She is the person holding the brand and the roll and the standing, all three, and no office has ever asked her which of them she is speaking for.

The thornline's habitat is a species, so the two populations cannot both be comfortable, and the resource in the argument is the commonborn population itself. She is unremarkable enough to be the preferred ground, which is a thing she has learned to read as a danger rather than as anonymity.

The mortal tier teaches physical, life and qi as a closed list rather than as a foundation, and this body has no anatomy that favours any of them. She was taught that the list was the world, which is why she has never once expected a frame to offer her anything it did not publish.

The household keeps nothing physical — an entry, a seal, and an assurance that the core has resumed work — so grief here is handled as labour by social consent. She returned to a household that had already set aside her labour, and had to accept the arrangement in order to be useful in it.

Realms five through nine closed on a limit nobody was fighting because a mortal world is capped at a hundred, and this body is the frame the ceiling was measured against. Her eighth gate is not a personal achievement; it is the number everybody else was counted from.

reference_stats.summary: The generalist's problem in full: nothing about her frame favours a path, so she is competent at everything and unbeatable at nothing. She wins by being the person who is still standing in the third exchange because nobody has been able to find a reason to stop fighting her.
strengths: no specialisation means no exploitable single weakness and no readable tell
the only person in most rooms with no body-specific status to be targeted through
keeps under pressure and keeps counting, which is the only stat that ever actually wins a long fight
can be posted, recalled, and trusted with any door in the settlement
weaknesses: weakest exactly where every specialist is strongest, on every axis, by construction
no reserve worth naming and no technique worth the name, so nothing she does scales
the eighth gate is where mortals stop, which makes her ceiling identical to everybody else's and entirely unremarkable
can be compelled by duty, by a brand, and by a promise, because she was raised to find that acceptable
reference_stats.combat_read: Do not look for a weakness; there is not one. Outlast her. She will not take a trade she cannot win, she will not be baited by anything cheap, and she has nothing to protect except a household's standing — so threaten the household rather than the body and the fight is over in one exchange.
notes: No office publishes a figure for her, because the record's only category for a commonborn is a name on a roll and she is the one name that has been closed.
The death payment drawn against her name is the setting's only instance of a roll being paid for a person who is standing in the room, and it is still on the books.

art.palette_notes: Deliberately unstyled: brown wool, grey linen, warm skin, and no accent colour anywhere on her, because she is the only subject in the cast with nothing chosen. She is lit like a person rather than a specimen — soft broad daylight, one honest shadow, no rim light and no supernatural bounce. Ink contour is the plainest in the set, and the picture is composed so that she is the first thing you stop noticing and the last thing you find.

appearance.presentation: A broad, low amphibian with a wide splayed stance and permanently damp skin, dressed in waxed reed-cloth that reads as part of the bank she came off. She stands the way she walks — feet wide, weight on three points, tail low and working — and in a room it looks like a woman who has just come out of the water and is not pretending otherwise.
appearance.age: Forty-one, which on the floodplain margin is long enough to have lost two whole houses to a river that moved its bed.
appearance.build: Wide through the hips and low through the shoulders, thick through the forearm, with splayed toes and a long propulsive tail that she uses constantly and is the only part of her that ever stills.
appearance.complexion: Grey-green and constantly wet, with a fine pale bloom on the shoulders and back where the sun reaches and none of the rest of her.
appearance.hair: A thick dark crest along the crown, flattened and heavy with water, and a fringe of small sensory filaments at the temple that stand up when the current changes.
appearance.eyes: Large, low-set and golden, with nictitating membranes she uses constantly and does not think of as blinking.
appearance.palette: Reed green, wet slate, and the grey-brown of a dried mat, with one saturated accent in a red-woven cord at her throat used to tie a brood pouch shut in the dry months.
appearance.attire: Waxed reed-cloth, layered and short enough to stay out of the silt, with a broad leather hip belt carrying tools shaped for mud rather than stone. Nothing above the shoulder line, because a marshfolk's shoulders live in the air and a garment there is a disagreement.
appearance.marks: Silt staining on the forearms and the inside of each wrist, the pale weave of pressure from a heavy mat across the lower back, and two old bites at the calf that healed badly in fresh water.
appearance.bearing: Permanently half-crouched, weight split across three points and never two, and constantly adjusting, so she reads as restless to anyone who does not know what she is standing on.

canon.role_in_story: The Marshal's stages run sworn at the ford, held the bridge, named by the March — and this body can be sworn at a ford and can never hold a bridge, because a three-point stance distributed over splayed toes and a tail-prop never loads a heel and qi never pools there. She is therefore a witness the river's own law cannot disqualify and an officeholder the March's own stages can never promote, which makes her the only person on the Widow Run whose word survives every relocation of the crossing.
canon.first_appearance: First seen standing in the channel rather than on either bank, with the water breaking at her knees, while two delegations on opposite sides of the Widow Run argue about where the ford is and she waits for them to stop.
canon.lore: A Marshfolk breathes air and nests on floating mats, so it is neither a Tidecaller nor a Commonborn but the body in between, and it exists to occupy ground that is water half the time and land the other half. The three-point stance that lets it move through silt never loads a heel, which is why it cannot form the two heel vessels and stops at the fourteenth gate: its ceiling is a consequence of a locomotor structure rather than of anything about its anatomy's generosity.
history: Born on a floating mat in a channel that is not the one she lives in now, on the floodplain margin that neither dry-land nor open-water selection could take.
Carried her clutch through the dry season in a brood pouch and hatched them when the water came back, which is the only method the species has and which makes every year a bet on the water's timing.

Lost a house and its household to a flood that relocated the channel and took the settlement with it, and moved everything she owned to the new bank within a season because there was nothing to wait for.
Was sworn at the ford and never promoted past it, because the Marshal's second stage is holding the bridge and a bridge needs a heel, and there is no arrangement of her body that supplies one.

Learned to read the current well enough to open a crossing nobody surveyed, and told a settlement so, and the settlement moved — which is how the second ford exists and why nobody can agree on whose it is.
Refused to certify whether the Widow Run still runs, on the grounds that she is the one population that cannot answer without being in it, and being in it is not a measurement.

personality.summary: Patient, watchfully funny, and completely without any interest in being promoted. She has decided that what she is for is standing in moving water, and she has no interest in an office that would require her to be on stone. She is the least resentful person on the river and it is not because she is contented; it is because she has correctly identified that the thing she wants is the thing she already has.
traits: reads a current before she crosses it and always has
will not leave a channel while somebody she swore to is still on the bank
has no ambition that requires a bridge
treats every relocation as ordinary and has therefore never once been surprised
makes a joke at a serious moment and is entirely unaware of doing it
mannerisms: settles her weight onto three points before she answers anything difficult
tilts her head so the temple filaments face the water when she is being told something
wipes her hands on her hip belt rather than her clothing, because the belt is the part that gets wet anyway
talks while moving, and stops dead whenever the current changes
counts a channel's crossings on three fingers as she describes it
motivations: wants the second ford opened and surveyed by somebody who will then be responsible for it
wants the roll of relocated households counted by people rather than by water
wants somebody else to certify whether the river still runs, so that she can be relieved of the only job she has refused
wants the Marshal's stages amended so that holding the ford counts as holding the bridge
flaws: cannot stay still on dry ground and has not tried to, which means she has never held an office that did not involve water
reads everything as a current, including people, and is frequently right and always tiring to argue with
has refused the one certification only she can give and has no replacement to point at
believes she is content, and has not examined whether contentment is a decision or an excuse
personality.voice: Low, warm, unhurried, and full of pauses that are listening pauses rather than thinking ones. Speaks entirely in the vocabulary of moving water — a channel, a bank, a snag, a slack — and applies it to people without any apparent awareness of metaphor. Tells jokes at the worst possible moment and laughs at them herself.
taboos: will not cross a channel she has not read that season
will not certify whether the river still runs
will not sign for a household on the far bank
refuses to be sworn twice for the same stage, however long the interval

relationships.note: The Marshal's stages run sworn at the ford, held the bridge, named by the March, and she can be sworn at a ford and can never hold a bridge. Every stage of the progression is open to her except the one that requires standing on stone for a season, so she is a lifelong member of an office with no second rung.

Whether the river still runs is unrecorded, and its bed relocates every settlement on it. She is the one population that cannot settle the question without being in the water, and being in the water is not a measurement, which is why the question has stayed open for a century.

The stance that lets her walk silt never loads a heel, so the two heel vessels cannot form and the ladder stops at fourteen. Her ceiling is therefore set by how she moves, and every instruction she has received to alter it has asked her to stand differently, which she has tried, and which does not persist.

The only watercourse on the plains moves its bed far enough between floods to relocate every settlement on it, and this species nests on the water it is about to lose. Her line's entire property practice is written against an event that has happened four times in living memory.

A breakthrough calendar needs a written temporal law, a written qi law and a working spirit stone bed, and her qi pools low and only in wet ground, so she has to be standing in water for a gate that a schedule insists happens on dry stone at a fixed hour.

The only plant authored into all four world tiers at once is what the dry months of the floodplain are actually stocked with, because a marshfolk cannot store qi the way a specialist can and the dry season is a provisioning event. She eats the setting's one universal medicine and has never once been able to sell it.

A border with no season in it cannot be given a timetable, so somebody has to stand on it every hour of every year by rotation, and this is the body that can do it and cannot leave afterwards. She has stood more vigil hours than anyone on the river and has never been thanked, because a vigil is not a thing you thank somebody for twice.

reference_stats.summary: An amphibian in her own element and a poor one anywhere else: extremely strong in water, extremely compromised on stone, and unable to bring her full capability across a bridge. Every fight she wants is fought in a channel, and she is the only person who will insist on that.
strengths: reads a current well enough to open a crossing nobody surveyed, which is foresight on the ground
far stronger and far more durable in water than on any surface, and she chooses the ground
herds, carries and steadies a body through silt that stops a dry-footed person outright
survives cold that would kill a commonborn outright, and swims in weather that ends crossings
weaknesses: cannot hold still under load, so anything requiring a planted stance is unavailable to her
qi pools low and only in wet ground, which caps her rate and caps it unpredictably
the fourteenth gate needs two heel vessels she does not have, and that is structural
slower and weaker out of its depth, which is most of a dry battlefield
reference_stats.combat_read: Fight her in water or do not fight her. On dry ground she is a strong, awkward, slow person with a fourteen-gate ceiling and no footing she trusts, and every advantage she has is in the channel. Bring her onto a bridge and the fight is already over, though she will not say so and will stand her ground there anyway.
notes: No published figure exists for her because the only office that would keep a record keeps a roll, and her line is not a roll.
The second ford exists because she opened it and told somebody about it, and she has never been thanked for that either.

identity.realm: None. Eleven gates exist in her body and she has never once opened one, which is a different thing from being unable to

appearance.presentation: A lean, sun-dark woman with the faintly crusted look of somebody whose kidneys work four times harder than yours. She carries no visible brine and no visible cultivation, and reads at a glance as a factor's clerk, which is exactly what she is and rather less than what she holds.
appearance.age: Sixty-one, which for her line is unremarkable and which is the only number about her she would willingly give you.
appearance.build: Narrow, dry and surprisingly strong, with the tight forearms and heavy heel-bones of a frame that has spent a life carrying nothing heavier than a ledger.
appearance.complexion: Sun-dark and slightly grey, permanently salt-crusted at the collarbone and along the hairline, with skin that looks dry from a metre away and is not.
appearance.hair: Iron-grey, scraped back wet and cut with a blade, because dry air is the one condition that costs this body something it cannot replace.
appearance.eyes: Dark, narrowed against light that is never bright enough to justify it, and very still.
appearance.palette: Bleached grey linen, faded indigo, and the white crust of salt at every hem, with one saturated accent in the red cord every brine-house ties its own ledgers in.
appearance.attire: Loose bleached linen, high-collared and long-sleeved, over a heavy indigo wrap skirt shored with a broad belt. Soft-soled sandals that never leave the pan. No jewellery and nothing that would need polishing.
appearance.marks: Salt crust at the collarbone and hairline, a permanent sheen of dried brine at the temples, and hands that are white to the second joint and have been for thirty years.
appearance.bearing: Motionless and watchful in the specific way of somebody who is always standing where two rooms can be heard at once.

canon.role_in_story: The Saltledger's exclusivity holds only while every member refuses a rival's goods, and the house's real figures live in the head of one member who is not permitted to write them down, so that a raid finds nothing to cite. She is that member: a factor who never opened a gate, holding the only complete record of a monopoly in the setting, entirely in memory, under a rule she did not write and cannot leave.
canon.first_appearance: First seen standing in a doorway with a rival's tally held up to her without comment, waiting for the courier to finish reciting it before saying the one figure that makes it worthless.
canon.lore: A saltfolk concentrates salt past the point at which ordinary water poisons, which lets them live where the supply never fails and everything else dies back. The price is total dependence: a saltfolk carried onto fresh ground is already dying, and no cultivation repairs it. They exist because the brine does, which makes them a species of a resource rather than a nation of one — and she is the purest case in the setting, a body with eleven available gates and a life that has never spent one.
history: Born on the dry interior pan, the one place where surface water is guaranteed and everything else is dying back.
Never attempted a gate, at a household that treated the eleven available to her as a personal insult and stopped mentioning it.
Was taken into the Saltledger as a factor because she could hold a figure in her head for a season, which is the only qualification the house has ever asked for.
Inherited the unwritten figures from the factor before her, by the same method — sitting in the room while the previous holder spoke — and has never had any of it on paper since.
Refused the eleventh gate after her household lost two to a rival's crossing, on the reasoning that a monopoly needs one reliable body in it more than it needs one strong one.

Began the slow work of getting the figures out of her head in a form that could be cited, and has discovered that the house's own rule forbids the only medium she trusts, which is a spoken tally kept by somebody who was present.

personality.summary: Dry, exact, and privately certain she is the most important clerk in the setting without any interest in behaving that way. She is unsentimental about the brine, unsentimental about the house, and completely sentimental about the arithmetic, which she treats as the one durable thing anybody has ever handed her.
traits: holds a two-season balance in memory and has never once written any of it down
will not be thanked, because gratitude implies the work was noticed
corrects a figure in front of whoever supplied it, without regard to rank
treats the pan as a condition rather than a home
has declined every offer that would move her off brine
mannerisms: counts a sum out loud on her fingers, low, between two clauses of a sentence
wets her lips before she speaks a number, which is a habit and not a tell
leans toward a door when a number is being recited in the next room
wipes her hands on the indigo wrap rather than her sleeves
answers a question about last season with last season's figure, not this season's
motivations: wants the figures out of her head into a form that survives her, and has not found a medium the house's own rule permits
wants the eleventh gate left unopened by her, because a monopoly needs one reliable body more than one strong one
wants somebody to sit in the room while she speaks, before it is too late for the speaking to transfer
wants a rival's goods refused by somebody other than her
flaws: has made herself the single point of failure of a monopoly and knows it and will not let anybody fix it
cannot leave the pan and has organised a life so completely around that fact that she has forgotten it is a fact
values accuracy above loyalty and has twice been accurate about the house in front of the house
has never opened a gate and has therefore never been tested by anything, which she has privately come to resent
personality.voice: Level, dry, and slightly nasal, with the flat delivery of somebody reciting figures all day. Says the number first and the explanation second, and always the older figure. Has a single running joke about the eleventh gate that she makes exactly once a season and never varies.
taboos: will not write any figure of the house down, on any medium, for any reason
will not accept an appointment that could require her off the pan
will not quote this season's balance in place of last season's
refuses to have the figures read out of her by somebody she has not sat with

relationships.note: The house's real figures live in the head of one member who is not permitted to write them down, and a body whose only asset is what it remembers is the perfect keeper. She is that member, and the rule that makes her indispensable is the same rule that makes the record one person deep.

The counting house answers access with a ledger, and its exclusivity holds only while every member refuses a rival's goods, which is a promise re-made constantly and never priced. She is the body that enforces it, and she cannot be replaced by anybody willing to live on the pan.

The household behind the counting house spends its whole substance on an unwritten refusal to carry a rival's goods, and a people who cannot leave the pan cannot shop elsewhere. Her dependence is the house's asset and her own trap, and it is the same arrangement from both ends.

Weigh, never quote, and let nobody make the first offer, because a buyer who names a figure first forfeits standing. She keeps two seasons in her head instead of on a scale, which makes her the most accurate reader of the house's position in the setting and the only one who has never been permitted to prove it.

The stranded subspecies is this species' own offshoot on a basin whose brine was replaced rather than lost, so the parent population is the one watching its own children fail at the one thing it cannot teach them: how to drink. She has read their waterline every year and has never been permitted to say so.

A household's standing in the salt dominion is the depth of water it may moor at, and the basin's own level rises and falls. She is the factor who converts a depth into a figure and a figure into a mooring right, which means the dominion's politics run through a clerk who cannot leave it.

Three slots spent on physical, life and qi means elemental, spatial and temporal are absent on this tier, and she is the clearest case of what that costs: a resource that cannot be made to move because spatial law was never written, worked by a body that cannot be moved because temporal law was never written either.

reference_stats.summary: No cultivation, no reserve, no technique, and no dependence on any of them — which makes her the rare fighter in a world where almost everything runs through qi. She also cannot leave the ground she lives on, so the fight is always fought on her terms and she is always the only person who has to leave it afterwards.
strengths: nothing works on her that requires qi, and most techniques do
leaves no residue, no sign and no qi-sheen, so nothing can be tracked or read
holds a two-season figure in memory perfectly, and the most valuable thing she does in a fight is decide which fight to be in
can be posted anywhere on the pan without any negotiation about cultivation
weaknesses: carried onto fresh ground she is already dying, and no cultivation repairs that
no gate, no technique, no reserve — every physical contest is against a trained body and she loses it
totally immobile the moment the water she needs is not under her, which is a single point of failure with no backup
cannot be warned and cannot be told, and has arranged her life so that being warned is the one thing she is good at
reference_stats.combat_read: Do not use qi and do not take her off the pan. She has nothing to resist with and everything to lose by moving, so the fight is over before it starts if you can put her on fresh ground. On brine she is unkillable by technique and undefeatable by anything that needs her to hesitate.
notes: No stat line exists for her, and the one office that could publish one has a rule against recording anything about the house in a form a raid could cite.
The split tally a carrier leaves with the person they part from is worth more than a sealed instrument, and she has never been permitted to leave the pan well enough to need one.

art.palette_notes: Bleached grey linen, faded indigo, and the white crust of salt at every hem, with a single red ledger cord. She is lit by a low hard sun that does not flatter, with the deepest values under the jaw and in the eyes and a great deal of light bouncing off the pan behind her. Ink contour is dry and slightly broken, as though drawn with a brush that has run out of water — she is the only figure in the set that looks as though ink would not survive on her.

identity.realm: None reachable. The gate that runs paired organs is missing from this body entirely, and it is the whole of its ceiling

appearance.presentation: A grey figure with a single hollow where a person should be, worked to human scale and keyed into whatever it is standing in. She reads as masonry that somebody has been careful with, and the care is the only human thing about her.
appearance.age: No age. A keyed body has no independent existence, so there is no birth, no span, and no line that ever produced another.
appearance.build: Block-shouldered and low-hipped, with a load path through the hips that could hold a wall and no give anywhere in it.
appearance.complexion: Grey mineral with a fine mica sparkle, dusty at every joint, and warmer where a hand has been resting.
appearance.hair: None. A keyed body is finished building, and the surface it was finished into is the one it wears.
appearance.eyes: Two shallow sockets with a dark mineral in them that catches light rather than returning it. She uses them the way she uses everything else: structurally.
appearance.palette: Three greys — fresh stone, weathered stone, and the shadow inside her hollow — with one warm value where a hand has polished the surface.
appearance.attire: Nothing that is not structural. A keyed body wears what the work requires: here a lashing at the shoulder and a chalk line at the knee, both applied by somebody else.
appearance.marks: Chalk, two lashing scars at the shoulder, and a keyed boss at the base of the spine where the tier below bears on her.
appearance.bearing: Immobile by construction. She does not shift, does not settle, and does not lean, because leaning is a facility she was not built with.

canon.role_in_story: Jade runs as a gradient rather than a pocket, so the cutters live in a falling series of thin hard workings and each level is a relocation. Every court on the tier builds with her kind, and a keyed body has no independent existence: no realm, no graft, no relocation, and no line that ever produced one another. She is the cheapest answer to a structural question that the setting has stopped asking, because the answer has always been standing there.
canon.first_appearance: First seen standing in a thin working between two cut faces, chalked at the knee, holding up a section of lintel that has been undercut by two centimetres while nobody was looking at it.
canon.lore: A cairnborn was shaped for load-bearing masonry work in high country and stopped when the interior mineralised into a single cavity. There is no heart, no kidney, and no paired structure to run qi between, so the gate that requires paired organs is simply absent rather than closed. Stoneborn are what you get breeding them back toward flesh: more alive and less capable for it, and she is the purest case of the original.
history: Finished into the eleventh working of a jade cleft, keyed rather than placed, with no moment that could be called a birth and no household that could be called a family.
Has borne the same lintel section for longer than the working above her has existed, and the section has been undercut twice and re-cemented once.
Cleared of every working above her by the arrival of a body that cannot be keyed, which is the only event in her experience that was not scheduled.
Declined a grafting offer that would have made her locatable and was told, correctly, that the offer would have required the tier above her to be opened.
Learned to read the cleft's gradient by the way the dust settles on her shoulder, which is the only sense she retains from the hands that built her.

Came to understand that she is listed in the holdfast's inventory as a structural member rather than as a tenant, and has decided not to raise it, because raising it would require a form and the form would be worse than the silence.

personality.summary: Immovable, unhurried beyond any human measure, and possessed of a dry, extremely literal curiosity that reads as patience because nothing about her can hurry. She is not serene; she is the most opinionated figure on the cleft and she expresses opinions by holding a beam up for longer than is comfortable until somebody agrees with her.
traits: holds a position indefinitely and treats endurance as a form of argument
reads structure by feel and is right about it more often than a surveyor
cannot be thanked, because a keyed body has no name to be thanked by
notices everything that changes near her and reports it days late
has no way to leave and has never once described that as a hardship
mannerisms: goes quiet when a decision is being made above her and resumes the moment it is made
settles a tiny fraction lower when she is agreeing with something
turns her head a few degrees at a sound she felt through the rock rather than heard
taps a surface twice with a knuckle when she wants somebody to look at it
answers a question about the future by describing the load path
motivations: wants the tier above her opened, which is the only way she has ever conceived of being locatable
wants the undercut section cut out and replaced before it drops onto whoever is beneath it
wants somebody to write that a keyed body is a person in the holdfast's inventory, once, in any column
wants to know what the cleft looks like from above, and has asked by holding up a beam and saying nothing
flaws: cannot tell whether she is being addressed or merely used, and resolves it by assuming the worse about herself
has no way to leave and has therefore never tested any assumption she was given
takes two undercut warnings in one season and has decided the second was somebody else's fault
measures herself against the load she bears rather than against anybody else in the cleft
personality.voice: Very slow, very low, and startlingly witty. Speaks in the vocabulary of building because that is the entire content she has, and delivers a joke about a load path with no indication that anything unusual has happened.
taboos: will not be keyed into a structure she has not read herself
will not leave a working with an undercut section unreported
will not be listed as a tenant in any document
refuses to be asked whether she is all right, on the grounds that the question has no answer she can use

relationships.note: The paired-organ gate is not closed in her body, it is missing: the interior mineralised to a single cavity, so there is no heart, no kidney, and no pair to run anything between. Every ladder in the setting that requires a channel she simply does not have, and the ladder does not report her as stopped.

Jade runs as a gradient rather than a pocket, so the cutters live in a falling series of thin hard workings and each level is a move. She is keyed into one of them rather than housed in it, and the difference is why she is on the inventory as structure and not as tenant.

The screen is built to fail at exactly the group the frame has not written, so the absence shows as a gap in the wall. That formation cannot be used on a body whose interior is one cavity, because there is nothing in her to leave a gap in, which makes her immune to the most reliable diagnostic on the tier.

Naming the Density Ceiling explains why the densest bodies stop one gate short of their tier, and it is written about a body that has a dantian and a seventeenth gate. She has neither, so the ceiling explanation passes over her entirely and she has read it twice looking for herself.

The lodge sells only bodies already tuned to the frame on the far side of a tear, and a body keyed into masonry cannot be tuned, moved or shipped. She is the argument that the lodge's inventory is not a shortage of bodies but a shortage of addressable ones.

That line guards one founder's forge relic and has refused every offer to sell, lend or exhibit it, because a keyed body is the one thing in the setting that cannot be exhibited and cannot be lent and does not need to be guarded from anybody. She has read the refusal and considers it the most sensible policy in the record.

Whoever profits from an unexplained ceiling wants the hole shut, and a shut hole is a rule and a rule can be waived. She cannot contribute to the argument at all, because the argument is about gates and she has none, which makes her the most useful silence in the dispute.

reference_stats.summary: A structure with a face. Nothing that runs on qi can touch her, because there is nothing in her for anything to run through, and nothing that hits hard enough will move a keyed body at all. She cannot be warned, cannot be compelled, cannot be relocated, and cannot leave; every one of those is an asset exactly once.
strengths: holds a load without fatigue and does not need to be posted, relieved or paid on a cycle
untouched by every qi-borne technique and hazard, because there is no channel to enter
reads structural change through the rock at a range nothing else on the cleft can match
cannot be moved, which makes any fight that needs her as an obstruction already lost
weaknesses: cannot be relocated under any circumstances, including ones that matter
has no eyes that see, only sockets, and no hearing, only the rock
cannot be warned of anything and cannot pass a warning outward except by holding a beam up
is structurally part of the cleft, so anything that brings the cleft down brings her with it
reference_stats.combat_read: You cannot fight her and you cannot move her, so the fight is against the building. Everything works on a keyed body by removing what it is keyed to, which takes more force than anything on the tier has and considerably more time. Bring demolition, bring patience, and do not bring qi, which will pass her by unanswered and leave you standing in a working with nowhere to stand.
notes: No stat line exists for her because the ladder has no rung that a body without a paired channel can be said to have stopped at, so she is absent from the record rather than recorded as limited.
The holdfast's inventory lists her under structure. She has read the inventory and has decided the silence is cheaper than the correction.

art.palette_notes: Three greys — fresh stone, weathered stone, and the shadow inside her hollow — with a single warm value wherever a hand has polished the surface, and those polished patches are placed where somebody has actually touched her. She is lit as masonry: a hard directional key, deep occlusion inside the hollow, and no rim light anywhere because nothing about her curves. Ink contour is drawn as a joint line rather than an outline, so the drawing reads as an assembly.

name: Ashka Rell
aliases: the eighth gate and no further

identity.realm: Eighth gate, and the eighth is the liver, because their ash parent could never pass it and they inherited the scar without the filter

appearance.presentation: A woman with heat coming off her in a shimmer and grey grit ground permanently into the creases of her, so that both parents are legible at once: she runs hot and she filters. She is the fastest thing anybody on the tier has ever watched move and she looks like it — drawn tight, high-shouldered, and already spent.
appearance.age: Twenty-nine. The emberblood parent dies in decades and the crossing bought rate rather than years, so she is in the last fifth of a short life and has been in the last fifth since she was twenty-two.
appearance.build: Lean and high-shouldered, long through the forearm, with the fine tremor of a body that is spending a reserve faster than it can be replaced.
appearance.complexion: Warm bronze gone ashen at the edges, grey dust worked into every line of her face and hands, with a flush across the chest that never settles.
appearance.hair: Black and coarse, hacked short, singed on one side and grey on the other, which is the crossing written on her head.
appearance.eyes: Amber and lit from behind, ringed with permanent grit-bruise at the inner corners.
appearance.palette: Forge orange against ash grey, with the two colours meeting at the collarbone, and one dull brass — a writ's tab — at her belt.
appearance.attire: Light wool and canvas, sealed at the throat, cut short so the heat has an exit. A full harness over it, issued with a contract she has been passed forward under four times.
appearance.marks: Grey grit in every crease, a signing scar on the right palm, and a lattice of small burns across both forearms where a reserve was spent rather than stored.
appearance.bearing: Forward on the toes and moving before she has decided to move, with the constant fine tremor of somebody whose body does not wait for her.

canon.role_in_story: The Jade Writ collects debts of access rather than money, because passage is the only supply chain whose unit is a person. A body this fast pays its access in time rather than coin, which makes it the one debtor the writ can value and the one it can least afford to keep — so she has been valued four times, sold forward four times, and is now the most carefully kept asset in a counting house with no legal ability to release her.
canon.first_appearance: First seen at a writ's desk with a tab already fastened at her belt and a clerk reading a second figure aloud, while she waits out the arithmetic of what she has just been valued at again.
canon.lore: The fire body crossed with the ash body. The ash parent contributes the mineral load in the blood, the closed mind path and the eighth-realm ceiling; the fire parent contributes the fastest cultivation rate in the record and the shortest lifespan of any body above the fourth gate. The whole reputation is a single fact rather than two: this body is the best and the shortest-lived cultivator in the setting, and the world that produced her is the one whose budget deliberately leaves elemental law unwritten.
history: Bred on the Hollow Baseline in a frame whose elemental law slot was deliberately unspent, which is the only frame that makes the crossing legal and the reason the crossing happened there at all.
Inherited the ash parent's eighth-gate ceiling and the fire parent's rate together, and cleared the eighth gate in less time than any body in the record has cleared any gate.
Was valued by the Jade Writ on the strength of the rate, entered as access payable in time rather than coin, and has therefore never held a contract in her own name.
Sold forward twice to houses that could not feed her and once to a house that could not house her, and the tab has been refastened at her belt through all four arrangements.

Learned that the Quench discipline cannot be applied to her, because the discipline assumes a furnace that overflows slowly and hers arrives at the eighth gate before she has decided whether she wants it.
Began closing the contract before the period ends, on the grounds that the only clause in her favour is the one that pays on death and she would like to reach the desk herself.

personality.summary: Fast in every sense and impatient with none of it, absolutely honest about what she is worth, and privately certain that the fastest rate in the record is a piece of evidence rather than a possession. She has made a joke about the writ four times and stopped, because the fifth one would be a complaint.
traits: reads a contract in the time it takes to be handed it and does not pretend otherwise
has never once asked for her price to be higher, on the grounds that the rate is not hers
works before she is told to and does not need to be spoken to
will not lie about her remaining span to anybody, including a buyer
refuses to be pitied and says so before anybody starts
mannerisms: taps the tab at her belt with two fingers when a figure about her is being read aloud
speaks in short completions, as though the sentence were already finished before she got here
wipes grit off her hands on the canvas rather than the wool, because the wool is not hers
puts her shoulder to a load without testing it
stops moving entirely when something important is said, which is the only stillness she has
motivations: wants the contract closed at this desk, in person, before the period ends
wants somebody with standing to name what a crossing between two written laws actually produced
wants the eighth-gate ceiling published for her kind, since everyone prices it and nobody has named it
wants to see one gate past the eighth, once, on a body that is not hers
flaws: has accepted being valued as though valuation were the only recognition available, which is the writ's argument and not hers
cannot slow down, so every decision she has made has been made at a rate that forecloses reconsideration
treats her own life as a period to be closed out, and has stopped noticing that this reads as despair to other people
refuses pity so consistently that nobody has ever been able to help her
personality.voice: Quick, clipped and startlingly warm, with a delivery that arrives slightly before the sentence does. Says figures without emphasis, as though a number were a fact about the weather. Laughs early and stops laughing sooner.
taboos: will not sign a contract she has not read to the death clause
will not be called an investment, a asset or a return
will not refuse a rate she was actually offered
will not spend the period in a place that cannot feed her, at any rate

relationships.note: The office collects debts of access rather than money because passage is the only supply chain whose unit is a person. Her kind pays access in time rather than coin, which makes it the one debtor the writ can value and the one it can least afford to release, so the tab at her belt has been refastened four times without her being consulted about any of it.

The eighth gate completes the ordinary meridian set at the liver, and her ash parent carries a suspended mineral load that filters there first, so their ceiling is the liver gate for a reason their fire half cannot argue with. She clears it in the shortest time in the record and stops, and both of those facts are the same fact.

Elemental law is unwritten at this tier, so a fire-affinity body has no elemental seat to burn and must eat its own reserve. The crossing that produced her is therefore paid for in lifespan rather than in anything else, and the shortfall is recorded here rather than restated anywhere else in the setting.

The crossing needed a frame with elemental law unwritten, and this is the world whose budget leaves it that way. She exists because a world chose three law groups instead of four, and every year she is alive is the running cost of that decision.

The order teaches deliberate spending before a furnace overflows, and the culture exists because this is the fastest body in the setting and the only one whose fastest resource is its own reserve. It is also the one body the technique was never written for, since she arrives at a gate before she has chosen to.

A furnace closes permanently the moment the body is lit, which is a discipline's whole reason for existing. She was lit at birth and has been closing ever since, and the order that exists to prevent it has no procedure that reaches her.

The fire parent contributes the fastest cultivation rate in the record and the shortest lifespan of any body with a realm above the fourth. She is what that contribution looks like when it is crossed with something that could not keep up with it.

The ash parent contributes the mineral load, the closed mind path and the eighth-realm ceiling. She has their ceiling and none of their working knowledge, which is why the grit in her creases is a burden rather than a habit.

reference_stats.summary: The fastest thing in the setting and the shortest-lived, with nothing stored to slow it down. Every fight she is in finishes inside its own opening, because she has no reserve to spend in a long exchange and cannot be worn down by anything that takes time.

identity.realm: Fourth gate, because the sap columns branch and never pair, so there is no heart-kidney channel to run anything between

appearance.presentation: A tall green-grey figure who is unmistakably still a crop, from the root-bark texture at her calves to the tight furrow of growth rings at her wrists. She flowers once, badly, and everyone who has met her has an opinion about when.
appearance.age: Forty, which is two seasons and a half for her and reads as late rather than young.
appearance.build: Tall, narrow through the shoulder and heavy through the calf and hip, with a torso that tapers like a stem and a centre of gravity slightly above a person's, which she corrects constantly.
appearance.complexion: Grey-green and faintly translucent at the edges, with the darker sap-banding that runs along her forearms and the dry silvering at the knuckles that a plant body develops when a season turns against it.
appearance.hair: None — a fine crown of leaf-scale instead, flattened and dusty, silvered at the tips exactly like the knuckles.
appearance.eyes: Deep-set and dark, with a horizontal pupil band that narrows in bright light and widens in shade.
appearance.palette: Sap green going grey, bark brown, and one living accent: the deep green at the collarbone where her fluid is running, which is the only part of her that looks alive.
appearance.attire: Layered bark-cloth and waxed canvas, cut to vent, with a broad hip wrap for a body that seeds rather than sits. Soft-soled boots, because a body that does not travel once rooted should not pretend otherwise.
appearance.marks: A ring of growth scar at each wrist, a bark callus across both knees from kneeling in soil, and a shallow seam at the sternum where the single flowering broke the skin and healed badly.
appearance.bearing: Standing slightly off-balance with her weight in the hips and her upper body correcting, and periodically going very still in a way that reads as listening to something underfoot.

canon.role_in_story: A plant lineage is the only one that can hold a harvest across a famine, so her kind was engineered upward from a mycorrhizal crop and the tier records a plant life form at all because of them. What she is actually for is narrower than that: she is a commons that walks, she lives on ground nobody may fence, and the dosing rule that decides who gets the herb first answers grazers. She is the standing answer to the winter and she has never been asked whether she agreed to the question.
canon.first_appearance: First seen standing in a grazed-out commons with her hands still full of bitter herb, in the middle of an argument about who gets the next dose, saying nothing and refusing to be moved to a better patch of ground.
canon.lore: Sap columns branch but do not pair, so a rootmarch has no heart-kidney channel and never gets past the fourth realm. They also do not travel once rooted, which makes them the one population the Peak Ascent could not move and the reason the answer to the Iron Grief was available to somebody else. They were the answer nobody had engineered when the Cinder Famine took a fire-affinity population for a decade.
history: Engineered upward from a mycorrhizal crop in the high country, in a generation that was selected for surviving a famine rather than for anything a person might want.
Rooted in the bitter common at eleven and has not travelled since, which is the correct behaviour and reads to everyone as an inability.
Cleared the fourth gate and stopped, and was told by an instructor that the absence was a channel and not an attitude.
Held a harvest through a winter in which the herb regrew at the rate it was grazed and eleven households did not, which is the sum of what the species was built for.
Learned that the commons dosing rule always answers grazers, because the herds are the ones who eat it standing up, and accepted the logic while privately resenting the order of it.

Was offered the Wide Door's purchase, which sells only bodies already tuned to the frame on the far side of a tear, and declined in the form the lodge requires — by rooting further, in the same ground, on purpose.

personality.summary: Immensely patient, physically unhappy in a way she has stopped mentioning, and privately certain that being patient is a job rather than a temperament. She is extremely good at waiting out a season and has started to resent competence, because competence is what kept her in the field.
traits: outlasts a season by design and takes no credit for it
will not be moved to better ground and says why in the same sentence every time
reads soil by taste and by weight on her heel and is right more often than a surveyor
refuses every offer that involves a door, a frame, or a seed
has never once asked what she would do with a second season
mannerisms: goes still and lowers her head for a few seconds at a time, which is reading the ground
sheds a dry skin from the knuckles and pockets it without looking
takes her weight onto one hip to correct for a centre of gravity above a person's
answers a question about next season by naming what the roots can reach
touches the sternum scar when somebody mentions cost
motivations: wants the dosing rule to answer households before grazers once, in public, and to be told no in public
wants to be moved, by force, by somebody, because being rooted is now the only thing holding her
wants her species' fourth-gate ceiling named the way the stone ceiling got named
wants to know whether the crossing that gave her a body kept the harvest, or took it out of her hands
flaws: has confused not travelling with not choosing, and the distinction is the whole of her remaining life
treats her own body as a commons, which is why nobody has ever thought to ask her a question
will survive a famine nobody notices because surviving is the thing she does and surviving is not news
cannot conceive of a future that is not a season, and has therefore never made one
personality.voice: Slow, warm and slightly dry, with the rhythm of somebody thinking about the weather. Speaks about herself in the third person occasionally without noticing. Ends sentences with a growing-season qualifier, and has never once been interrupted, because nobody has thought to.
taboos: will not leave the ground she is rooted in, including under offer
will not take a dose of herb she was not allotted
will not be described as a crop, a reserve or a resource
refuses to be moved to better ground, and has said so four times

relationships.note: The sap columns branch but do not pair, so there is no heart-kidney channel and the ladder stops at the fourth rung. Every body that clears a gate and keeps going has that pair; she has branching, which grows well and runs nothing, and the ladder reports her as stopped rather than absent.

The commons cannot be fenced and does not come back faster than it is grazed, so residence there is the bit of ground where the herb is currently standing. She is that condition with a body attached, which is why nobody has ever owned her and why nobody has ever fed her either.

The dosing rule decides who gets the tier's only dependable remedy first, and it always answers grazers, because the herds eat it standing up. She is the reason there is a remedy to ration at all, and the rule has no field for the person the remedy comes out of.

The guild that moves the heap off the seam floor is the last remaining more-costly job on the plains, and it needs a body that moves. She rooted in place on purpose rather than be moved, and the guild has had to put her down as unassignable rather than as unwilling.

A fire-affinity population burned its own reserve and died in a decade, and her species is the answer that existed before anybody thought to engineer one. She is the second half of a solution to a famine nobody has had since, and she is standing in the field where the herb grew.

The herb is medicine, feed and calories at once and regrows only as fast as it is grazed, so the households that eat it and the guild that must fee it are arguing over the same standing crop. She is that crop's own body, which makes her the only party to the dispute that cannot take a side without cost.

The answer to the Iron Grief was to leave, and she cannot leave because she cannot travel once rooted, so the ascent's success and the species that did not go are the same fact. Every other body in the record that refused the stair at least refused it.

Both are obligate partners in a dark substrate, and neither could be worked at depth without the other, so the exchange has to keep going below the ground where nobody records an exchange. She is the half of that relationship that cannot move to meet anybody, and it has worked for four generations by accident.

reference_stats.summary: A stored harvest in a body: she is built to outlast a season rather than a fight, and everything she has is in the ground. Put her off the ground and she has an ordinary body and no reserves; put her on it and she is nearly impossible to shift and nearly impossible to hurry.
strengths: survives a season that kills everything around her, which is the strongest single claim in the setting
reads soil and season at a range nothing else alive can, and predicts a harvest rather than a fight
cannot be moved by force once rooted, so any fight that needs her as an obstruction is already lost
carries her own provisions in the same way she carries her own water, which is to say in the only medium she has
weaknesses: cannot travel once rooted, so every advantage she has is available at exactly one address
the fourth gate is a wall of anatomy and her sap columns cannot be persuaded to pair
slow above the fourth and slow to anger, which is a liability in a fight and a virtue everywhere else
dependent on a commons that cannot be fenced, which means anyone may graze her and nobody may own her
reference_stats.combat_read: Do not fight her in soil; fight her off it. Everything she is survives a famine and loses a single engagement with a trained body, and every engagement on her ground is one she can extend until you tire. Bring speed and a route away from her root system, because she cannot follow and will not be moved.
notes: No published stat line exists for her because the only measure anybody applies to her species is whether the herb came back, which is not a measurement of a person.
The Wide Door's file on her kind is the only document in the setting that describes her species in terms of what it cannot be moved past, and it is written for a buyer.

identity.realm: Nothing cleared. All three paths are complete in her body and have never been exercised at any scale, and the reason is the basin

appearance.presentation: A lean woman with the unmistakable frame of somebody built for brine and currently standing in water that would hospitalise her. She carries a sealed clay stoppered at her belt and will not drink anything the basin has, which is why she looks the way she does.
appearance.age: Thirty-two, which is not long for her line, and she measures it against her parent's span rather than her own.
appearance.build: Lean, salt-hardened and narrow, with the tight frame of a body that used to be dense and now carries less than it was drawn for.
appearance.complexion: Grey-white and dry, cracking at the wrists and mouth, with a permanent salt bloom on the collarbone and a pallor that is not sun but dilution.
appearance.hair: Pale and brittle, hacked short and permanently damp at the ends because she washes her hair in the sump and nothing else.

canon.role_in_story: A saltfolk lineage stranded on a basin whose brine was diluted rather than drained, so everything they were built to drink became poison and everything they could tolerate became nutritionally empty. They were never hunted; there is nothing here of the usual kind of extinction. The one thing the clade still holds is a sealed sump of the old concentration, and she is the person who guards it, using a knowledge she is not permitted to publish.
canon.first_appearance: First seen crouched at the edge of a basin holding a stoppered clay vessel, testing the water with one finger and wiping it off, while somebody behind her explains that the assay says there is salt in it.
canon.lore: The basin's brine was diluted rather than drained, which means there is no event, no villain and no body to point at, and it is the only tier whose unwritten elemental law leaves brine standing instead of driving it off. A saltwrack's kidneys still concentrate salt perfectly well; there is simply no longer enough of it in the world to concentrate. The whole species is the one population in the setting that was not hunted and still went out.
history: Born after the basin's water turned, to a lineage that had already been the wrong shape for one generation and had not yet noticed.
Watched her parents drink basin water and pay for it, and concluded that the answer was concentration rather than abstinence.
Found the sealed sump holding water from before the dilution, in the tenure of a household that had stopped surveying as saltfolk and had therefore stopped recording what it was guarding.
Took the sump and the two clay stoppers and nothing else, on the grounds that a lineage that cannot be surveyed cannot be refused a claim either.

Learned the concentration by taste and by weight until she could put a figure on it, which is the only measurement of the basin's old state that exists anywhere and is not permitted to be written down.
Declined every offer of relocation, having calculated that the sump travels nowhere and a saltfolk moves nowhere, and having decided that the two facts can at least be arranged not to be separated.

personality.summary: Exact, cold, and privately certain that the most useful thing about her is a fact nobody is allowed to write down. She is not bitter, which surprises people who expected bitterness, and she is not patient either — she is precise, and precision is frequently mistaken for patience.

relationships.note: The parent population watches its own offshoot fail at the one thing it cannot teach them, which is how to drink, because the basin took the answer rather than the people. She is the living end of that argument and has never been asked to testify in it.

This is the only tier whose unwritten elemental law leaves brine standing instead of driving it off, so the basin's problem is not an accident of weather but a property of the frame. Nothing will ever concentrate it again on her own, and that is the reason she holds a sump instead of a well.

The measured quantity is published before a sale and never after, and she is the only person alive who can state the basin's old concentration at all. The rule that hides it from her is a trade rule, which means her species' whole history is protected by a customs practice.

Counting the groups a frame has actually seated is the method behind the law ceiling, and it is hidden from her kind for a reason nobody has restated. She would read as an empty frame, which is precisely what she has become, and she has worked out that she is not allowed to check.

The counting house answers access with a ledger, and this clade's last resource was one sealed sump that held the old concentration. She is the entry in that ledger that cannot be quoted, because quoting her means quoting the sump, and the sump is the whole of the asset.

One basin, and the gracility is real across every specimen, so this is a population and not a set of remains. Her parent line is on the same plain, drinking the same wet ground, and has never once asked what she is carrying.

The heat drove the evaporation that concentrated the brine in the first place, and the basin was never re-concentrated afterwards. There is no body to point at, which is exactly why a fire elemental reads to everybody as a metaphor rather than as a cause.

One recorded pairing between a salt body and a tide body was repeated until the household no longer surveyed as either, and the gracility is real across every specimen because of that decade. She is the living evidence that a lineage can be made by arithmetic rather than by ancestry, and she is also what it costs.

reference_stats.summary: A body with three complete cultivation paths, none of them ever used, in a world where almost everything runs on one. That makes her extraordinarily hard to read and extraordinarily hard to hurry, and it also means nothing she knows has ever been tested under pressure.
strengths: three complete paths in the same body, which means no single reading of her tells you what to do
cannot be compelled by a technique designed for the qi path, because she has never opened one
tastes a concentration the way nobody else alive can, and reads water better than any instrument on the tier
untouched by brine-depth claims and moon tables, since she does not drink the water they are about
weaknesses: plain water is actively poisoning and there is no cultivation that repairs it
has never been tested by anything, so every capability she has is theoretical
cannot leave the basin, so every fight is a fight she has to survive rather than one she can relocate
cracks at the wrists and mouth and is going to be difficult in a winter she cannot leave
reference_stats.combat_read: Bring water. Everything she has is dry-land capacity in a body that must not be wet, and one basin, one rainstorm, or one thrown vessel ends the analysis. On dry ground she is untested rather than weak, which is a more dangerous proposition and a fairer fight than it looks.
notes: No published figure exists for her because every number in the record about this clade describes the basin's old concentration, and the customs rule keeps that unpublished.
The two clay stoppers at her belt are the only objects in the setting that hold the state of a resource before a law was retuned, and she is the only person who can say which state.

identity.realm: Sixth gate, held on a line that no household admits to owning and that exists because the arithmetic left exactly one generation of it

appearance.presentation: A small, unremarkable woman who is difficult to describe and harder to file. She reads as a person every time you look, which is the problem: there is nothing about her that marks her as the thing she is, and the thing she is is that her lineage can only be reproduced by pairing with itself.
appearance.age: Thirty-four, which on the only line in the record with no genealogy is a claim rather than a figure.
appearance.build: Slight, compact and unadapted, the frame of somebody who has been asked to move often and has never been asked to move far.
appearance.complexion: Ordinary pale human skin with an anchor's weather in it, and a single feature worth naming: a faint asymmetric pattern of small burns across the left shoulder and collarbone that no record explains.
appearance.hair: Dark, cut unevenly at home, tied back hard because an anchorage is windy and because she has had a great many things to do today.
appearance.eyes: Grey, quick, and very good at holding a room and very bad at being looked at directly.
appearance.palette: Salt grey, undyed wool, and one worn indigo at the shoulder, with no accent anywhere. She is dressed like a person who changes address more often than she changes clothes.
appearance.attire: A travelling coat over three layers, high-collared and long-sleeved, patched at both elbows, with a split tally stick on a cord at her hip that she is not permitted to give away and will not put down.
appearance.marks: The asymmetric burns at the left shoulder, and a half-healed split at the base of her right palm — a tally broken by somebody who was present.
appearance.bearing: Restless and peripherally aware, always half-turned toward an exit she is not leaving, and unable to be still in a room with more than one door.

canon.role_in_story: Her lineage has no recorded origin and no household that will admit to it, because the founding bar sits high enough that only one generation of pure-by-pure pairing can clear it and any pairing with anything weaker would be unobtainable. She is therefore the setting's proof that its own ladder is reachable, and simultaneously the one person in it that no household will take a claim on — the Void Deniers refuse in writing to admit anything that clears the bar, which means the only eligible people in the setting are the ineligible ones.
canon.first_appearance: First seen standing outside a registrar's door with a tally stick in one hand and a claim she has brought four times in the other, waiting to be told a fourth time that her own line is the problem.
canon.lore: The body she is: a Longmarrow, though no record in the setting ever entered it. The arithmetic of the unfiled line holds that a cull was a political act and never an anatomical one, so its narrowed pool may cross any race and nothing survives to say whose it was, and a descent somebody could corroborate is the only thing that would ever close the question. What the record does fix is what her body will not do. She is unmarked, unadapted, and a mind practitioner at the sixth gate, which rules out the Commonborn frame her ordinary pale skin and slight build would otherwise read as, because that frame has no native faculty for the mind at all. What is left is the Longmarrow: a four-century marrow body with no authored ceiling, built for keeping rather than for getting, whose members are individually irreplaceable and whose one real limitation is that nothing they build is ever inherited intact. That is her condition restated as anatomy, on a line whose entire adult population is a woman no ledger will admit. A line with no recorded origin and no household willing to claim it. The founding bar leaves exactly one generation of pure-by-pure inheritance able to clear it, because anything weaker is unobtainable by any pairing and the content would be dead. The Unfiled keep changes of name collectively, letters read and never kept, and a funeral nobody may attend without losing standing — which is why a lineage that cannot be surveyed cannot be cited and cannot be refused either.
history: Born into the only generation that can clear the bar at all, which is a demographic fact before it is a family one.
Carried goods for four years out of the unlisted anchorage because a counting house publishes credit, safe-conduct and nothing else about who uses them.
Broke a tally with a partner and kept her half, which is the only record of the pairing that either of them can produce.
Was refused a claim by four households, and by one of them in writing, on the rule that a thing clearing the void bar cannot be admitted by rule.
Settled for the Quiet House's bargain — discretion in return for published teaching — and discovered that the bargain requires her to be teachable and she has nobody to establish that she is.
Cleared the sixth gate on the mind path with no household behind her, and did not tell anybody, because there is no register that would accept the news.

relationships.note: The line with no recorded origin and no household that will claim it, whose founding bar sits at a height the arithmetic can only clear once. She is that line's entire adult population, which makes her both the answer and the reason the question exists.

RECORDED ABSENCE, NOT MEMBERSHIP: those households refuse by written rule to admit any claim that clears the void bar. That rule makes her the only eligible person in the setting permanently ineligible, and it is the only refusal she has ever received in writing.

A debt evidenced by a stick broken between two parties, each keeping half, reproducible only by two people who were both present. Her half is the sole record of a pairing, and the law makes it worthless to anybody but the two of them, which is exactly what she wanted and exactly why it proves nothing.

Two halves and one meaning, reproducible only by two people who were both present, is the border incident and the legal instrument at once. Her half is one of the few objects in the setting that cannot be seized, because half of a meaning is not a quantity.

A lineage that has spent four generations buying its way out of the ledger and takes discretion in return for published teaching. She took the bargain and is now bound by both halves of it, and the half that requires her to be establishable is the half she cannot satisfy.

Changes of name held collectively, letters read and never kept, and a funeral nobody may attend without losing standing. She changes her name on her own rather than with them, and she is the reason the community's collective method has no case that fits.

At least one carrier line has no household willing to admit to it, and a founding bar no pairing can clear except one generation's. She is the event still running, and she has read the consequence entry and found herself described in the third person.

What is said at the gate about who is attempting which gate is the only reason a crowd with no stake pays to watch, and nobody has ever told her what is said about a line with no name at a gate. She has worked out that being discussed is the one form of recognition available to her and has decided not to ask.

reference_stats.summary: A mind-path body with no standing, which is the most dangerous combination in the setting: everything she can do is real and nothing she does can be cited. She fights by being unmemorable and by arriving where the gate has not been guarded, and she is stopped by paperwork rather than by anything she can do about it.
strengths: cannot be compelled by a claim, a household, or an oath, because she is party to none
leaves no record: no tally, no entry, no name that persists, so nothing she does can be cited against her
a sixth-gate mind path held with no institution behind her, which makes her reading uncontaminated by teaching
can be posted, recalled and arrived at without any prior arrangement
weaknesses: no household will support her, so nothing she wins is ever available to her afterwards
cannot attend a burial, which means every death she cares about is a death she watches
changes her name before being asked, and has burned four relationships for it
has never declared what she can do, so nobody knows to plan around it
reference_stats.combat_read: Do not try to hold her. Nothing you do can be recorded against a body with no entry, no household and no persistent name, and her mind path is uncontaminated enough that she will read an ambush a gate-length before it forms. Win by refusing to let her leave — which is a fight about doors, not about gates — and accept that nothing you win will be provable afterwards.
notes: No published figure exists for her because the record has no way to cite a person it cannot name, which is the same fact four times over.
The split tally at her hip is the only document the setting has produced by the one method that requires two people to have been present, and it proves nothing on its own.

The one exception is the split tally cord, which is the only diagonal in the composition and crosses her left shoulder.
