identity.realm: Eleventh gate, reached on a defensive continuous fire rather than a stored one, which is a slower burn and not a bigger tank

appearance.presentation: A broad, banked woman who radiates at a temperature you can stand beside without flinching, which is the whole of what her kind is for and the reason nobody can tell her and a forge apart. She looks like a person who has been standing in a doorway for forty years.
appearance.age: Forty-four on a span that runs to fifty, and she has the settled look of somebody who has made a bargain with that.
appearance.build: Heavy through the chest and forearms, thick-dermed and slow to heat, with the deep reserve of a frame built to lose heat continuously rather than to store it.
appearance.complexion: Warm bronze shot through with mineral grey, greying at the temples and along the forearms, and warm to the touch everywhere without ever being hot.
appearance.hair: Black going iron, thick and worn long, because a body that sheds heat needs a head covering and the household supplies one as a matter of course.
appearance.eyes: Amber, steady, and lit from behind by a very low and very constant glow rather than a furnace behind them.
appearance.palette: Banked orange at the collarbone fading to mineral grey at the extremities, undyed wool and oiled leather, and one bright value: the Cradle's hearth-ash mark at the shoulder.
appearance.attire: Heavy layered wool over oiled leather, high-collared and long-sleeved, with a broad sash of grey hearth-ash worn over the left shoulder because that is where a Cradle member's mark goes and where the light is weakest.
appearance.marks: The hearth-ash mark at the left shoulder, a mineral grey band across both forearms where the fire half has been held down for four decades, and no scarring anywhere else at all.
appearance.bearing: Still, low, and enormously difficult to hurry, radiating a heat that makes the air around her move and that she has never once apologised for.

canon.role_in_story: The founding concentration descends from a single mineral-fire crossing made once at a founding, and the household has held the result as one unbroken thread ever since. The grant is defensive and continuous rather than large, because their home air is stone and a fire that must be banked high is a fire that goes out. She is the last working member of that thread, and the thread's continuity rule and her body's requirement point in opposite directions.
canon.first_appearance: First seen standing in a doorway between two rooms at different temperatures, radiating into the colder one, while somebody inside explains that the fire must be banked and she does not move and does not speak.
canon.lore: The body she is: an Emberblood. The Ember Cradle names its members as that line, and the mineral-fire crossing it made once at a founding is held alongside the line rather than beneath it — the pressure-resistance in the descendant is the only half of the crossing that survived, and a thin concentration cannot be spent twice. The span confirms it independently of any household: Emberblood is authored at fifty years, she is forty-four on a span that runs to fifty, and the one office that prices a mortal term rather than a weight quotes her household's at fifty. What she is not is the other half of that one conception. Stonebound is the mineral frame carrying a genuine fire circulation — denser than either parent, dying at about sixty years, stopped at the fourth gate for want of a second organ — while she is the fire parent, warm to the touch everywhere without ever being hot, thick-dermed and slow to heat, and the density is what doubles the fire parent's lifespan rather than what she is made of; the mineral grey shot through her complexion is the crossing showing, not the frame. Emberblood closes the mind path the moment the furnace is lit and nothing else, so her body path is not merely legal but the only one her line has: a body that cannot bank high and must spend continuously is her whole discipline, and the fifty years pay for it in gates she never gets. A line from the founding generation of a body that burned through its own reserve and kept going, recorded alongside the stone line because the two were crossed at the same conception and have stayed crossed since. That is why the concentration is thin and unevenly spread. Their gift is a slower burn rather than a bigger tank: nothing here lands harder and everything here lasts, which on a body with a fifty-year span is the same as a strategy.
history: Born to the Cradle's unbroken thread in Flame Valley, the one valley whose air is stone enough that a fire body has to defend itself continuously.
Was told at fourteen that the thread's continuity requires no crossing out, and did not ask what that left out, because nobody in the household had.
Learned to hold a continuous low fire indefinitely, which took four years and cost her the ceiling a banked flame would have reached.
Cleared the eleventh gate on that fire, which is one short of what her span would have supported, and stopped, and knows exactly which of the two costs was hers.
Refused a crossing-out that the household offered as a kindness, on the grounds that accepting it ends the thread and the thread is the only thing anybody here is proud of.
Came to understand that the household's pride and her own requirement are the same rule read from two sides, and that she is the reason it cannot be relaxed, and that this is not a complaint.

personality.summary: Unhurried to a degree that reads as simple, warm in a way that is literally her body temperature, and privately aware that she is an argument her household is making without intending to. She is not resentful and she is not serene; she has simply got very good at holding a fire and has run out of other subjects.

relationships.note: The household made the one crossing between a burning body and a mineral one and has held the result as a single thin thread ever since. She is that thread's last working member, and a thread's continuity rule is the reason she cannot leave.

The founding concentration descends from this household's first signed burn. A fire body with no seated elemental law has no budget and must burn its own reserve, so the whole of her line's discipline is a signature made before anybody knew what it would cost.

Children are raised on the graded route itself by whichever household holds the term, so that nobody belongs to a place. She was raised on a route and belongs to a thread, and the two arrangements are incompatible in a way nobody thought about until she was fourteen.

A branch culled under debt climbed the ridge and came back with enough standing to claim the charter's narrowed line. Hers is the line that would have to be narrowed to make room, and she has read the claim and has said nothing about it, which the returning branch has noticed.

The order teaches deliberate spending before a furnace overflows. She has been taught the opposite discipline for four decades — spend nothing, spend constantly, never bank — and it has worked, which is the most unsettling thing anybody has ever been able to say about the order.

The first resource priced by period rather than by weight, because a mortal lifespan inside the immortal world is a fixed term and upkeep rises fortyfold. Her kind's term is fifty years, which makes every higher tier a lease rather than a purchase, and she is a lease that keeps paying.

The public account holds that realms three and four failed for want of will rather than more, and this line's founding grant is the evidence against it — a body that kept going by choosing a slower burn is exactly the record that disproves the account, and the account is the one nobody has read.

The fire parent donates the throughput and nothing else, and the density doubles the fire parent's lifespan. Their whole relationship is one conception held for four decades on both sides, and neither half has ever been able to explain the other to a third person.

reference_stats.summary: Nothing about her lands hard and everything about her lasts. She cannot be knocked back and cannot be finished quickly, and she trades both of those against a ceiling one gate short of what her span would support — which is a body optimised for a long siege inside a small room.
strengths: sustained output with no peak, so any exchange that favours the dramatic one exchange goes against her
a continuous defensive heat that degrades every cold and qi-borne approach before it arrives
does not tire, does not flare, and cannot be baited into spending anything
so difficult to hurry that most tactics resolve into nothing happening to her
weaknesses: cannot bank a flame, so every gate she might have reached is a gate she gave up for stability
a fifty-year span, and she is in the last sixth of it
everything she has is close-range: there is no version of this that wins a long chase
immobilising her means moving her, and moving her means the thread ends
reference_stats.combat_read: Do not attack her. Everything that lands hard is wasted, because she has traded all of that for the ability to still be there in the fourth hour. Make the room colder, or make the fight a chase, or wait for a gate she never reached — those are the three ways. Anything that needs her to spend will be waiting for a spend that will not come.
notes: No published figure exists for her, because the Cradle's own records measure a founding thread by whether it is unbroken rather than by anything the body can do.
The hearth-ash mark at her shoulder is a membership sign and, because the fire is continuous, the only part of her that is always at the same temperature and therefore always legible.

identity.realm: None. Her grant is the default concentration found in long-settled households, and most of it never crosses its bar

appearance.presentation: A woman of exactly the right amount of everything, so consistently that people finish her sentences about herself and then cannot remember doing it. She reads as the person a room was expecting rather than the person who walked into it.
appearance.age: Fifty-one, which is unremarkable, and the whole of her life has been unremarkable, which is a different fact.
appearance.build: Unremarkable and unspecialised, the frame of a household that has been averaging whatever came into it for four centuries and has never once been asked to do anything else.
appearance.complexion: Ordinary warm human skin with nothing on it that any record has ever mentioned.
appearance.hair: Brown going grey, cut to a length that is fine, in a colour that is fine, and it has been the same for thirty years.
appearance.eyes: Brown, level, and easy to look away from, which is a description of a face rather than a verdict on one.
appearance.palette: Undifferentiated wool, brown and grey, with no accent she has chosen and one she inherited.
appearance.attire: Household wool, mended and well made, in a colour that four generations of her line have all been willing to wear. A cloth apron with a figure in a hand nobody now remembers.
appearance.marks: None worth recording. One burn on the inside of the left wrist from a hearth she was too young to be careful of.
appearance.bearing: Unremarkable and settled, and slightly too still to be interesting, and she has made a life out of that and has never been asked whether she wanted to.

canon.role_in_story: The Hearth Common carries the most ordinary concentration in the setting and has no bloodline of its own, only a habit of averaging whatever the household took in. Most actors hold some of it and most never cross its bar, which makes her the reference point that everything unusual in a settlement is measured against without anybody deciding to build one. She keeps the Standing Name's promise, so the average of a settlement is re-made in public once a year by the one person it is guaranteed to be accurate about.
canon.first_appearance: First seen standing in a plain meeting room beside a trestle table, already looking at the person who has just come in, having arrived early and in the same chair she always takes.
canon.lore: The body she is: a Commonborn, and that is the household's own account of itself rather than an inference from it. The Hearth Common records that the ordinary body is the one it averages into itself, and a house whose only distinction is its reliability has to be everywhere because nowhere is it exceptional — its members are never exceptional in any direction, which is her entire standing. The span confirms it: the Commonborn frame is authored at a hundred years and a ceiling of eight, and her own record calls her a hundred-year body twice, once where the concentration's smallness reads as a strategy and once where the same hundred years reads as a liability. What she is not is the long line she is averaged with. Longmarrow is four centuries of marrow-stored frame built for keeping rather than getting, and at fifty-one she would be a child on it; its one real limit is that nothing it builds is ever inherited intact, which is the exact opposite of a woman who has re-made the average of a settlement in public once a year for twenty years running. Nor is she Echoless. That body carries no meridian, no dantian and no qi and closes all three paths, so nothing could ever have been offered to her, and the refusal she describes — one cultivation instruction, refused because it would have cost her the mornings — requires a body that has something to refuse. That leaves her path legal twice over: she has no path seated at all, so no species can close the one she is not on. A lineage carried carefully for four centuries in long-settled households, averaged with whatever else the household took in. Common as a reading and unsurprising as a reading: most actors hold some and most never cross its bar. Its grant is small and on purpose, and the line is common because it is dependable rather than strong — which on a body that lives a hundred years is a strategy rather than a defect, provided nobody asks it to be extraordinary.
history: Born into the Hearth Common's averaging, which is not a bloodline but a habit, so nobody in the household could have told her what she would be.
Grew up being described as dependable, and believed it, and has since discovered that dependable is a thing people say instead of useful.
Took the Standing Name's keeping at thirty-one because the previous holder died and there was nobody else in the household who was already in the room every day.
Refused the one cultivation instruction she was ever offered, on the grounds that it would have cost her the mornings, and has never described that as a decision about power.
Read the Stair School's prospectus in person and was not admitted, on the published basis that it teaches to visitors and she was not going to visit.

Discovered in her forties that she has been the thing four hundred people compared themselves against without ever being named, and has decided that the correct response is to go on turning up and to say so once.

personality.summary: Steady, unresentful in a way she has had to work at, and privately aware that being the average is a job and that nobody has ever given her a day off from it. She is not self-pitying; she is a woman with an extraordinary talent for being the same as everybody and no use at all for it.

relationships.note: A community's promise is re-made jointly once a year and never priced, and it is the only insurance available to a population with no wealth. She has kept it for twenty years and has not once been late, and the society's whole function depends on somebody being exactly that unremarkable every single year.

The household carries the most ordinary concentration in the setting and has no bloodline of its own, only a habit of averaging whatever came in. Its dependability is measured against the same commons it eats, so the one population guaranteed never to fail is also the one guaranteed never to be asked for anything.

The only school on the plains that has never produced a graduate who lives there, because it teaches to visitors. She read the prospectus in person and was not admitted on the published basis, which is the most accurate description of her own position anybody in the setting has ever published.

A line carried carefully across four centuries belongs to a household with a four-century memory, and nothing about this one suggests an inwardness. Its grant is small on purpose, and the two lines ended up in the same households often enough that the average stopped being predictable.

After the Iron Grief the ground changed hands faster than the tally could follow, so a debt is evidenced by a stick broken between two parties, each keeping half. She has broken more of these than anybody in the settlement and has never once been the half that was lost.

Nobody here expects to ascend and the work is judged by what survives the season. That judgement is why the average is a success in this setting rather than a failure, and she is the only person who has had to make that argument from the inside.

The Widow Run opened a crossing nobody surveyed, and the two sides are a settlement that convenes where it knows the ford is and a chartered town at the stair foot. She has been seated at both tables and has never once been asked which one is hers, because either answer would have made her remarkable.

The commons's dependability is measured against the herb, because the herb regrows only as fast as it is grazed and everything else about a settlement is judged by the same figure. Her whole line's reliability is denominated in a plant, which is the most honest description of her standing that exists.

reference_stats.summary: No path, no reserve, and no surprises. Everything she has is the absence of a weakness: there is nothing here to aim at, nothing to read, and nothing to counter, which makes her extremely hard to fight and impossible to bet on.
strengths: untouched by anything that requires reading a body for a tell, because there is nothing to read
cannot be compelled, bribed or frightened, since no technique reaches a frame with no channel
always where she said she would be, which makes any plan that depends on her hold
no cultivation means nothing to detect, nothing to track and nothing to steal
weaknesses: no gate, no technique, no reserve: every physical contest is against a trained body and she loses it
cannot be warned of anything and has never once been in a position to warn anybody

reference_stats.combat_read: There is nothing to counter, so do not try to counter it. Everything physical ends quickly and she has no defence at all; the only exploitable thing about her is that she will not leave a room before a promise is re-made, and everybody who knows her knows it. Everything else is a person who cannot be frightened and cannot be hurried.
notes: No stat line exists for her, and the setting has never published a baseline against which a person could be read as average — which is the one measurement her entire line exists to provide.
The figure on her apron is in a hand nobody now remembers, which is the most honest possible emblem for a household that has averaged everything it was given.

name: Vell Orry
aliases: the ceiling that belongs to somebody else

identity.realm: Eighth gate, and she did not reach it: the colony stops there and the host inherits the stop

appearance.presentation: A weathered woman with a fine dark thorn-pattern visible under the skin of her forearms and throat, who reads as ill rather than as inhabited until you count the marks and then she reads as neither. She moves her hands carefully and does not appear to know why.
appearance.age: Fifty-three, which is long for the configuration she carries and short for the clan that keeps it.
appearance.build: Ordinary frame, thin through the shoulders, with the forearms slightly swollen where the thorn lines have thickened and the wrists noticeably colder than the rest of her.
appearance.complexion: Grey-pale and uneven, with a fine reticulate dark line running up from each wrist to the elbow and a second, finer set at the throat that is not quite skin and not quite anything else.
appearance.hair: Grey and coarse, cut short because the colony finds long roots, which she learned young and has never explained.
appearance.eyes: Brown, steady, and slightly too focused — the colony takes the broad field and leaves her the narrow one.
appearance.palette: Ash grey, iron brown, and one living value: the dark green-black of the thorn lines themselves where the light catches them at the throat.
appearance.attire: Loose undyed wool over a long linen shift, high-collared and long-sleeved, with a heavy belt she uses to brace her hands against. Nothing tight at the wrist, nothing that presses the lines.
appearance.marks: The thorn lines, both sets, which are the whole of her appearance and are the reason the mortuary college has no procedure for her.
appearance.bearing: Careful, unhurried and faintly fussy, with a habit of resting both hands on a surface rather than letting them hang.

canon.role_in_story: She is the one configuration in which a thornline colony and a host both reach old age, and the pairing is treated as one legal person in the only jurisdiction that has ruled on it. The colony stops at the eighth gate and the host inherits that stop, so her ceiling is her parasite's — which is the entire legal problem stated as a number. She is enrolled at the Gap School because its method is to seat a law and then move a student somewhere that law is missing, and the law missing in her is the one she carries.
canon.first_appearance: First seen sitting in the academy's diff-chamber with both hands flat on the bench, being asked by the second-year whether she would mind removing the collar so the reading can be taken properly, and not answering for a long time.
canon.lore: A thornline colony contributes the ceiling, the routing and a closed mind path, all inherited rather than authored. The host contributes the frame, the throughput and the only reachable registry, and neither half is anatomically dominant. The colony finishes only inside a living host, so this body has no homeland and is a range rather than a destination — and a body arriving where a required law group is unwritten is injured rather than slowed, which is this body's capital offence and its ordinary condition.
history: Was paired as an infant, by the clan that holds a share of a living thorn line, in the only configuration in which both halves reach old age.
Cleared nothing. The colony stopped at the eighth gate and she inherited the stop without ever reaching it, and has spent her life below a ceiling that belongs to something else.
Learned young that long roots give the colony somewhere to finish, and cut her hair at ten for reasons nobody explained to her.
Was entered as one legal person with the colony, in one jurisdiction, and discovered that this means her deaths cannot be certified and her growth cannot be measured by two different bodies.

Enrolled at the Gap School because it is the only institution that would seat a law and then send her somewhere that law is missing, which is a description of her own condition rather than a metaphor.
Refused the school's offer to run a technique on her, on the grounds that two frameworks at once is its capital offence and that the school would be documenting the offence rather than preventing it.
Began keeping her own readings of the two frameworks side by side and refusing to merge them, which nobody has ever asked her to stop doing.

personality.summary: Fussy, precise, and much harder to argue with than she looks. She has spent fifty years being the second half of a legal person and has developed an unusually strong position on the difference between what she is and what she is recorded as, which she is happy to explain at length to anyone who has not asked.

Runs on when talking about procedure. Stops dead when talking about the colony.

relationships.note: The colony stops at the eighth gate and the host inherits that stop, so her ceiling is the parasite's. She has never reached the eighth gate and has spent fifty years below it, and the ladder reports her as stopped rather than as carrying somebody else's ceiling.

The colony contributes the ceiling, the routing and a closed mind path, all inherited rather than authored, and it finishes only inside a living host. That is why this body has no homeland and is a range rather than a destination, and why the setting records the pairing as a range and not a place.

A clan whose kinship is a partnership rather than a descent, the host holding a share of a living thorn line and the colony holding the host. She is the asset in that arrangement and has never once been asked whether she considers it an asset.

The academy teaches by seating a law and then moving the student somewhere that law is missing, and this body's host is missing the law. She is not a metaphor for its method; she is an instance of it, which is the reason the method has a hole in it.

Running a technique on a group the frame has not written injures the body rather than slowing it, and that is this body's capital offence and its ordinary condition. Everything anybody has ever tried on her has worked at full strength and done damage in proportion.

Every sworn member of the sect who holds no office sits at the open door in all but name, and this species is the setting's only natural candidate for that post. She has been asked to take it four times and has refused on the grounds that the door is a job and she is a condition.

The last unworked iron is the only reason anybody settles ground that cannot be measured, and settlement density is host density. She is on that ground because it cannot be surveyed, which is the only citizenship she has ever been able to obtain.

The college reads the dead as the frame said and not as the village remembers, and separating those two memories is its whole function. She has no procedure in it, because the colony's growth and her growth are two readings of one body and the form has one field.

reference_stats.summary: Two frameworks reading one body at once, which means she can do things no single body can and cannot be hit by anything that assumes one set of channels. She is not a hybrid so much as a body with an unreliable second opinion about itself.
strengths: the colony's routing reads threats and arrivals that a single frame would miss, so she is never surprised
reads her own limits accurately enough to lose on paper before she loses on the ground
untouchable by anything that requires one consistent channel, because she has two and neither closes
does not tire in the way a body tires, because two frameworks share the load
weaknesses: the inherited eighth-gate stop means she has never been able to advance regardless of condition
anything run on her works at full strength and injures her in proportion, which is the worst possible trade
hands go cold without warning, which is a combat liability and a medical one
cannot be certified, cross-referenced, or recalled by any procedure, so help arrives only if somebody decides to bring it
reference_stats.combat_read: Do not use technique. It runs at full strength on her and injures her, so the conventional answer is the wrong one. Fight her with bodies, speed, and reach, and be aware that the colony reads your approach before you commit — everything about her is a warning system, and the only counter is to make two approaches at once.
notes: No stat line exists for her, because every figure the record could publish would describe one of two frameworks and the form has no way to say which.
The two records she keeps side by side are the only complete measurement of this configuration in the setting, and neither of them has ever been read by a person who was not her.

art.palette_notes: Ash grey and iron brown, with one living value — the dark green-black of the thorn lines at her throat and forearms, which is the only saturated colour in the picture and is drawn as translucency rather than as paint. She is lit flatly and coolly, because the colony takes the broad field of vision and the composition gives it to her shadow rather than to her face. Ink contour is doubled along the arms, following the lines, so the drawing reads as two things drawn over one another.

appearance.presentation: A tall, deep-bodied woman with the saltwater look of somebody whose line was made to last rather than to hit, and who looks about ten years younger than the four centuries of her name. Nothing about her is quick.
appearance.age: One hundred and forty, which is young for the line and which the line reads as a reason to keep her.
appearance.build: Tall, long, and enormously deep through the ribs, with a frame that expands under load rather than springing, and cold hands that are usually wet.
appearance.complexion: Cool brown with a permanent salt sheen at the collarbone and temples, weathered smooth rather than lined.
appearance.hair: Very dark and very long, worn in one heavy rope braid down the back with jade rings at three points, which is the line's own practice and not a fashion.
appearance.eyes: Deep-set, dark, and extremely patient, with a slight downward focus that everybody in her line has and which reads as good temper.
appearance.palette: Deep sea-green and wet slate, with three jade rings as the only warm value and the only ornament permitted in the Keep.
appearance.attire: Heavy sea-cloth over oiled wool, high-collared and long-sleeved, cut for pressure rather than for speed, with a weight belt at the waist and nothing fast on her at all.
appearance.marks: A pale band at the hairline where the braid sits, salt sheen at the temples, and no scarring anywhere on her body, which in a line this old is a discipline and not luck.
appearance.bearing: Slow, enormous, and completely unmovable once she has begun, with a habit of settling her weight before she agrees to anything.

canon.role_in_story: The oldest recorded carrier line in the setting, kept in one household so long that the name stopped describing a family and started describing a body. Two generations of pure pairing is the most this line has ever held, and the bar sits exactly there because that is the ceiling of an unbroken chain. She is the reason that number has never been three, which means she is simultaneously the Keep's greatest asset and the single reason it cannot grow.
canon.first_appearance: First seen standing in a doorway with her weight already settled and a three-ring braid over one shoulder, listening to a conversation about a third generation that she is not part of and has not corrected.
canon.lore: The body under the line is a Tidecaller, which is the whole of what the Tideborn record means: that entry carries the race id, and a Tidecaller is a long-lived body built for perception rather than force, holding water affinity and nothing else. The salt sheen at her collarbone, the cold hands that are usually wet, and the four centuries the Keep has carried the name are therefore one fact and not three. One hundred and forty is young on a hundred-and-sixty-year span, and the line reads her as young for it, which is a different thing from being early. Two generations of pure pairing is the authored bar, and the documented salt-water crossing is what a non-pure pairing would produce. Their grant trades immediate impact for sustained pressure: nothing here lands harder and everything here lasts. That is a strategy on a hundred-and-forty-year body and a liability on a fifty-year one, which is precisely why the Keep keeps them and nobody else can.
history: Was born into the Tideborn Keep at a point where the household was already a name rather than a family, and was entered as a carrier line before she could be entered as a child.
Cleared the thirteenth gate on sustained pressure over years rather than impact over minutes, which is the method the line's grant dictates and the only one any of them has ever used.
Learned at nineteen that the bar permits exactly two generations and that she is the second, which makes her simultaneously the most important member of the line and the reason there is no third.
Was offered a crossing-out that would have ended the chain and refused it, on the grounds that the chain is the only thing the household is and a crossing-out is permanent.
Declined the Quiet House's bargain because its discretion clause would have made her breeding, rather than her work, the thing kept private.
Has begun refusing to be weighed, on the argument that a figure published about a two-generation line becomes the reason a third is attempted.

personality.summary: Immovable, unhurriable, and much cleverer than the line's reputation for dependability suggests. She has spent her life being the reason a rule exists and has quietly, patiently, thoroughly stopped believing in the rule.

relationships.note: The one household that has held the oldest recorded carrier line so long that the name stopped describing a family and started describing a body. Two generations of pure pairing is the most it has ever held, and the founding bar sits exactly there because that is the ceiling of an unbroken chain — so she is the Keep's whole argument and its whole limit.

One recorded pairing between a salt body and a tide body was repeated until the household no longer surveyed as either. That documented crossing is what a non-pure pairing produces, and it is the reason this line has held at two generations rather than three.

The crown reads one figure against a ceiling and the March reads another against a lower one, so absolute standing puts the crown first and relative standing puts the March first. She is a body whose value is entirely relative, which is the whole dispute stated as a person.

A debt evidenced by a stick broken between two parties, each keeping half, which a court will sometimes prefer to an instrument. She has never entered one, on the grounds that an unbroken chain should not be able to owe anybody a debt proved by a broken object.

Two competent surveys of the same ground now disagree by more than the ground and none of the books is readable. Her line's grant is pressure rather than impact, and the only survey of what it does was written by people who measured for impact, so the record and the body do not talk.

A branch culled under debt came back with enough standing to claim the charter's narrowed line. Her line has never been narrowed because it has never been split, which means the whole mechanism that produced a rival has never once been tested against her.

Exclusivity holds only while every member refuses a rival's goods, and this is the line whose house refuses even inside its own house. She carries for the Saltledger and has never quoted a figure for it, because a chain that is quoted becomes a chain that is priced.

The unbounded office of a house that hands out load and not edge and recognises no stat at all, which a bloodline whose principal asset is continuity can hold without ever being measured. She is the setting's clearest reason an office can exist with no instrument at all.

reference_stats.summary: Nothing about her lands hard and everything about her lasts. She is a siege body with no peak and a hundred-and-forty-year span, which on a tier where the fastest bodies die at fifty is a structural advantage rather than a temperament.
strengths: sustained output with no peak, so any fight that rewards the decisive exchange goes against her
an enormous frame that expands under load rather than failing, so she can be leaned on indefinitely
no reserve worth stealing and no speed to pressure, so she cannot be rushed at all
long enough-lived that a wound that would end a shorter body is an inconvenience to hers
weaknesses: cannot cross out, cannot be measured, and cannot be quoted, so nothing she wins is ever formally hers
no peak means no burst: she loses every exchange that ends in one
the thirteenth gate is the line's ceiling and she has climbed it by a method that takes years
cannot be rescued quickly, because help arrives only if somebody decides to bring it and nobody is obliged
reference_stats.combat_read: Do not try to break her; there is no peak to break. Bring many opponents and give the fight time, because every hour is a trade you are worse at. The only real counters are reach and patience against her, and the truth is that a long fight in this setting is her engagement and not yours.
notes: No published figure exists for her, on her own request and to everyone's agreement, because a chain of two is a number and a person is not.
The three jade rings at the braid are the only ornament permitted in the Keep, which is itself an ornament count, which is the kind of detail a two-generation line can afford to be precious about.

art.palette_notes: Deep sea-green and wet slate, with three jade rings as the only warm value and the only ornament in the composition. identity.realm: None. Every child in this household is bound to a named debt before first breath, and hers named a branch that was removed to pay it

appearance.presentation: A wiry, unfinished-looking woman with the concentrated look of somebody who was grown for one purpose and the purpose came early. She reads as an instrument that has been tuned and not yet given anything to play.
appearance.age: Twenty-six, which in a household that culls on arithmetic is described as a good year.
appearance.build: Lean, low-shouldered and quick, with narrow hands and a frame that has clearly never been asked to carry anything but itself.
appearance.complexion: Cool pale skin with a faint sheen of salt at the collarbone, and the particular pallor of somebody who was raised indoors on somebody else's arithmetic.
appearance.hair: Dark and very straight, hacked to the jaw with a blade in the same four lengths every generation, because a household that concentrates does not waste on a style.
appearance.eyes: Grey, level, and extraordinarily clear — a concentration read outward rather than inward, which is the visible sign of the thing the household was keeping.
appearance.palette: Wet slate, undyed linen, and one cold accent — the white cord every debt-bound child in the household is tied with at first breath, still on her wrist.
appearance.attire: Bleached linen, high-collared and long-sleeved, over a plain heavy belt, with hard shoes and nothing that is hers rather than issued. The wrist cord is the only thing she has ever chosen not to remove.
appearance.marks: The debt cord at the left wrist, worn to a flat pale band, and the first cold-shock mark on both palms from a winter she was not expected to survive.
appearance.bearing: Still and alert, with the readiness of somebody who has been told since childhood that she is the part of the household that pays.

canon.role_in_story: Households culled their own branches to stop paying for siblings and kept the surviving line by binding every child to a named debt before first breath was drawn cold. She is the branch that was kept, and she was kept for one reason: concentration. A line held pure inside one household concentrates faster, so she was grown as an asset and the household's own accounting is what makes her valuable and what would make her disposable in a bad year.
canon.first_appearance: First seen standing outside a household door with a debt cord at her wrist and a list of names in her head, waiting to be told which of them she is being sent to replace.
canon.lore: The body she is: a Commonborn, which the house never wrote down, because the line she belongs to crosses races freely and the debt culture it produced is recorded as holding exactly two bodies, the Commonborn and the Emberblood. Hers is the first of those rather than the second, and her own skin says so: cool and pale, with a sheen at the collarbone that is salt and not heat, on a body that never had a furnace lit in it. The hundred-year span is the arithmetic underneath the cull as well, because a line that never dies of old age while breeding can always afford to settle its debts by paying for siblings instead. A tideculled body descends from a house that culled its own branches rather than marrying out of them, because a line held pure inside one household concentrates faster, and the Branch Cull was the decree that made it arithmetic rather than policy. Every household reaches it independently. She is the concentration itself: thirty-one living members where forty were, every one of them signed, and the debt she is named against is a branch rather than a sum.
history: Was signed at first breath to a named debt that was not a sum of money but a branch of the household removed to pay an earlier one.
Grew up inside a household of thirty-one where there had been forty, which nobody in it was permitted to call a cull and every member understood.
Was told at fourteen that the reason she existed is that the line concentrates, and believed it, and has since worked out that it also means there is only one of her.
Was refused the one cultivation instruction her household could afford, because a concentrated line spends its budget on the whole and not on a member.
Learned at nineteen that her named debt can be cleared only by a branch of her own body, which is the household's accounting arriving at its own conclusion.
Refused the instruction on a debt she could discharge, and has spent seven years being asked, by every member of her household, to reconsider.

personality.summary: Clipped, watchful, and far more dangerous than she has ever been given credit for, which she resents in a way that reads as modesty and is not. She has been grown for a purpose, knows exactly what it is, and has made one decision about it and will make no others.

personality.voice: Short, level, and clipped in a way that sounds like anger and is not. Answers in figures. Uses the household's own vocabulary — branch, column, bound, cleared — and has never once used a word from outside it except when refusing something.

will not speak a dead member's name as anything other than a name

relationships.note: Houses that could not fund a cultivator's ascent culled their own branches, and where an ascent is funded out of the branch's own lifetime the cull is arithmetic rather than policy and every household reaches it independently. She is the line that was kept by that arithmetic, and she is the reason it works.

Every child is bound to a named debt before first breath because a line held pure inside one household concentrates faster. The binding is not cruel and it is not a punishment; it is the mechanism, and it means she has never once been free to say no to anything and has never once been told she could.

A house that culled its own branches rather than marrying out of them, because concentration inside one household is faster. It is the body such a house is made of: a population that crosses nothing and therefore never dilutes, and which reaches its ceiling by refusing to spread.

A mortuary college keeps one sealed case for every death it cannot certify, and certifying a death needs a body. Her household's cull produced a generation whose burials were household business rather than college business, and she has the names and the college has none of them.

A branch culled under debt climbed the ridge and came back with enough standing to claim the charter's narrowed line. Her household has never been culled from, which is the only reason it has never had to face this, and she has read the case and understands exactly which clause would apply to her.

A founding bar no pairing can clear except one generation's means some lines only survive by being extremely narrow. She is what such a line looks like when it works: thirty-one people, one debt, and a concentration that four culls made possible.

Exclusivity holds only while every member refuses a rival's goods, and her household has never carried for a counting house and never will. She has been offered a berth twice and refused it twice, on her own account rather than the household's, which is the only independent decision she has made.

A debt evidenced by a stick broken between two parties, each keeping half, is worth more than a sealed instrument because it needs two people who were both present. Hers is named against a branch rather than a sum, so there is no second party to break a stick with, which is the cleanest possible description of her refusal.

reference_stats.summary: A concentrated body with no cultivation and no debt cleared: fast, unarmoured, and entirely unbound in the way that matters, which is to say she answers to nothing but a column in a household ledger. There is no peak in her and no reserve and no technique, so she wins by position and by not being where the ledger expects her.
strengths: no cultivation means nothing to detect, nothing to bind and nothing to track
fast and wiry, with a frame that has never been asked to carry a load and has never been dulled by one
cannot be compelled by a debt, because the only debt naming her is one she has refused three times to settle
can recite a household's whole debit column, which is the most useful and least obvious thing anybody has ever needed
weaknesses: no gate, no reserve, no technique: every physical contest against a trained body is lost
one person carrying a line's concentration is one point of failure, which she knows and cannot mitigate
has never been trained at anything, including fighting, and the household has said so in writing
cannot leave without either clearing a debt she cannot clear or becoming the branch that pays it
reference_stats.combat_read: There is no defence here at all, so the fight is about position. She is faster and smaller than anything she will meet, and completely unbound, so she wins by being somewhere the household's accounting does not look. Bring weight and reach and close the exits; do not bring qi, which has nothing to take hold of in her.
notes: No stat line exists for her, because the household that records her has no reason to and the college that would has no name to enter.
She can name every member the household removed and every year it removed them, which makes her the most complete record of a cull in the setting and the only one nobody has ever asked to read.
